findings.summary: Soundness: the append-only rule matches only imperative edit phrasings. It does not refuse the real criterion of job 20261102-005332-8gkv, the very instance the request cites, so the class is not prevented.
findings.evidence: The recorded 8gkv reading (evidence snapshot, records/jobs/2026-11/20261102-005332-8gkv/reading-1.json) has criterion 5: 'CHANGELOG.md has an entry ... ; docs/decisions.md D87 notes the exclusion.', plus a Modify deliverable of docs/decisions.md. On the candidate build, `cargo run -q -p athena-cli -- check-reading --request .../8gkv/request.json --reading .../8gkv/reading-1.json` prints `accept`. Rules i-iv need an edit verb in verb position before an id, 'append/add to Dnn', 'Dnn is <participle>', or 'existing entry' plus 'in place'. A declarative content criterion such as 'D87 notes/states/says/mentions X' passes, and that is how readers normally write content criteria. The corpus cases claim the recorded criterion 'was not available', but the snapshot holds it. Simpler and more correct: refuse a criterion that names docs/decisions.md (or the decision log) and an existing decision id unless it also says the id is cited, amended or superseded by a new or appended decision. Add the recorded 8gkv criterion as a corpus case. Optionally, as the 8gkv introspection proposed, tell the producer the log is append-only and have it run the guard.

summary: The candidate adds `check_judging_rules` as the last `step!` of `refusing_check`, adds a 13th reader rule, appends D174 and adds a CHANGELOG entry. I ran the targeted tests: the athena-core judging unit tests, the refusal corpus, the reader-brief test, the budgets test and the decisions guard all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks also passed. So every listed criterion is met as written. The verdict is still fail, on one major soundness finding. The request asks for the class to be prevented, and I ran the candidate's own `athena check-reading` on the real reading of job 20261102-005332-8gkv from the evidence snapshot. It prints `accept`. That reading's criterion 'docs/decisions.md D87 notes the exclusion' is the in-place edit that caused the rejection, and it passes because the matching only catches imperative phrasings ('edit D87', 'append to D87', 'D87 is rewritten'). Its tests use made-up or modelled texts and claim the recorded criterion was unavailable, but it is in the snapshot. Two minor findings: a loosened reading-rules size baseline and a possible false positive on 'fix/change the Dnn ...'. One nit: a planned test name does not match the added test.
